mainTopic: Engaging children on ליל הסדר, שמחת יום טוב with wine, and the size of the רביעית
overview: This amud begins with ways to keep children awake and curious on ליל הסדר. Adults hand out roasted grains and nuts, as רבי עקיבא himself did, and רבי אליעזר says we 'grab' the מצות so the children stay alert and ask questions. A ברייתא adds that רבי עקיבא ended his learning early only on ערב פסח, for the children, and on ערב יום הכיפורים, so his students would feed their children. Next, a ברייתא teaches that a person must make his household happy on יום טוב, based on 'ושמחת בחגך.' The תנא קמא says this is done with wine. רבי יהודה says each person gets what suits them: wine for men, and new clothing for women. רבי יהודה בן בתירא adds that when the בית המקדש stood, שמחה was through eating שלמים meat, and today it is through wine. The גמרא then defines the רביעית, the minimum cup of wine, using known vessels from ציפורי and טבריה and רב חסדא's measurement in fingerbreadths. It begins a ברייתא about the size of a מקוה to support רב חסדא, and that calculation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Giving children roasted grains and nuts on ערב פסח
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא: we give children roasted grains and nuts on ערב פסח so they stay awake and ask questions at the סדר.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We hand out] roasted grains and nuts on ערב פסח, so that [the children] will not fall asleep, and so that they will ask.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא that started on the previous page. It teaches a practice for keeping children interested on פסח night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is twofold. The treats keep the children awake, and the unusual treat makes them curious enough to ask questions. That sets the stage for telling the story of יציאת מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before פסח, leading into the סדר night
So that they will not fall asleep
And so that they will ask (questions)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new statement. It finishes a ברייתא ("מחלקין קליות ואגוזין לתינוקות") that began on the previous עמוד. That is why the sentence seems to start without a subject.

phrases.english: Roasted grains and nuts on Passover eve
phrases.notes: This finishes the line from the previous page: we hand out roasted grains and nuts to the children on Passover eve.

phrases.english: so that they will not sleep, and so that they will ask.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא begun on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children are given roasted grains and nuts on ערב פסח to keep them awake and get them asking questions.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא practiced this himself
steps.stepSummary: A report that רבי עקיבא personally handed out roasted grains and nuts to children on ערב פסח, for the same reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי עקיבא that he used to hand out roasted grains and nuts to children on ערב פסח, so that they would not fall asleep, and so that they would ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The text backs up the practice from step 1 with a real-life example from רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is added here. A great תנא is shown actually doing this, which confirms that the practice was put into action and taken seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: They said about him (a formula introducing a report of a sage's conduct)

phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Akiva
that he would distribute roasted grains and nuts
to children on Passover eve
so that they would not sleep, and so that they would ask.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁהָיָה מְחַלֵּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 with the conduct of a sage
steps.raayaObject: The practice of giving children treats on ערב פסח
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reported personal practice of רבי עקיבא

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: grab the מצות so the children stay awake
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר teaches that on פסח night we 'grab' the מצות, so that the children do not fall asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says, we grab the מצות on פסח nights for the sake of the children, so that they will not fall asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא gives a different method of keeping the children awake, from רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of treats, רבי אליעזר's method uses the pace and look of the meal. 'Grabbing' the מצות means eating quickly, or (per some מפרשים) snatching the plate away. Either way, the children notice something unusual, stay alert, and ask.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
We grab / snatch (eat quickly or remove hastily)

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One grabs the matzot on the nights of Passover
for the sake of the children, so that they will not sleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another method serving the same goal as step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצות are 'grabbed' on סדר night to keep the children awake and curious.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the custom of doing unusual things at the סדר (and is linked by some to hiding the אפיקומן) to engage children.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא only ended learning early on two days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that רבי עקיבא never announced the end of a learning session, except on ערב פסח and ערב יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: They said about רבי עקיבא that in all his days he never said, 'The time has come to get up' in the בית המדרש, except on the eves of פסח and the eve of יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The text brings another ברייתא about רבי עקיבא. It states the fact first and gives the reasons in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally רבי עקיבא let learning continue as long as students wanted. Two days were exceptions. This sets up the question of why exactly those days, which the next step answers.

keyTerms.meaning: The time has come to stand up (end the session)

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: It was taught: They said about Rabbi Akiva:
In all his days he never said
'The time has come to arise' in the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מֵעַרְבֵי פְסָחִים וְעֶרֶב יוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: except for the eves of Passover and the eve of Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: מִיָּמָיו לֹא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another report about רבי עקיבא, connected to the theme of children on ערב פסח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא ended learning early only on ערב פסח and ערב יום הכיפורים.

steps.title: The reasons for רבי עקיבא's two exceptions
steps.stepSummary: On ערב פסח he stopped so the children would not fall asleep at the סדר. On ערב יום הכיפורים he stopped so parents would feed their children.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב פסח — for the sake of the children, so that they will not fall asleep. And on ערב יום הכיפורים — so that they will feed their children.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why each of the two days was an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב פסח, ending early let families get home in time. The children could rest and start the סדר without falling asleep. On ערב יום הכיפורים, students needed time to feed their families before the fast. In both cases, the children's needs came before extra learning time.
steps.whatToRemember: Both reports about רבי עקיבא show the same value: caring for children's needs on these special days came even before extended Torah learning.

phrases.english: On the eve of Passover —
for the sake of the children, so that they would not sleep.
And the eve of Yom Kippur —
so that they would feed their children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the exceptions listed in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ערב פסח for the children's alertness at the סדר; ערב יום הכיפורים so parents could feed their children before the fast
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא stopped early on ערב פסח so the children would not fall asleep at the סדר, and on ערב יום הכיפורים so his students would feed their children.

steps.title: Obligation to make one's household happy on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a person must make his children and household happy on יום טוב, based on the פסוק 'ושמחת בחגך.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A person is obligated to make his children and the members of his household happy on the festival, as it says: 'And you shall rejoice in your festival.'
steps.whatsHappening: The text moves to a new but related topic: the general מצוה of שמחת יום טוב, which includes one's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים goes on to list one's son, daughter, and others. That shows the joy is not only personal: the head of the house must actively make his family happy. This links to the wine of the סדר, the topic surrounding this section.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall rejoice in your festival' (דברים ט״ז:י״ד)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A person is obligated to gladden
his children and household members on the Festival,
as it is stated: 'And you shall rejoice on your Festival.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חַיָּיב אָדָם לְשַׂמֵּחַ בָּנָיו וּבְנֵי בֵיתוֹ בָּרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from children at the סדר to the broader obligation of household joy on יום טוב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must make his children and household happy on יום טוב, derived from 'ושמחת בחגך.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the halachic obligation of שמחת יום טוב toward one's family, quoted in the רמב״ם and שולחן ערוך.

steps.title: The first opinion: make them happy with wine
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how one makes the household happy and answers: with wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what does he make them happy? With wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a short practical question about how to fulfill the obligation and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gives one answer for the whole household: wine. This becomes the position that רבי יהודה will refine in the next step.

phrases.english: With what does he gladden them? With wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how to carry out the obligation stated in step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What means one uses to make the household happy

steps.title: רבי יהודה: each group gets what suits them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says men should be made happy with what suits men, and women with what suits women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Men with what is fitting for them, and women with what is fitting for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the single answer of 'wine for everyone' and gives a more tailored approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is not about whether the obligation exists. It is about how to fulfill it. For רבי יהודה, real joy depends on what actually makes each person happy, so one item cannot fit everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: With what is fitting/suitable for them

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Men with what is fit for them,
and women with what is fit for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲנָשִׁים בָּרָאוּי לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the תנא קמא's 'wine for all'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each member of the household is made happy with what suits them.

steps.title: Men with wine, but what about women?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's view is spelled out: for men, wine. The question is then raised of what is fitting for women.
steps.simpleTranslation: Men with what is fitting for them — with wine. And women, with what?
steps.whatsHappening: The text explains the men's part of רבי יהודה's rule and then asks what the women's part means, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For men, רבי יהודה agrees with the תנא קמא that wine is the means. The open question is what counts as 'fitting' for women, and that needs a further source.

phrases.english: Men with what is fit for them — with wine.
And women, with what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the terms of רבי יהודה's statement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the 'fitting' means of joy for women according to רבי יהודה

steps.title: רב יוסף: women are made happy with new clothing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches that women are made happy with clothing: colored garments in בבל, pressed linen garments in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: In בבל — with colored clothes; in ארץ ישראל — with pressed linen clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question: for women, the fitting joy is new clothing, which depends on local fashion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer confirms רבי יהודה's idea that joy depends on what people actually value. Even the type of clothing changes by place: colorful fabrics were prized in בבל, and fine pressed linen in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees one must make the household happy on יום טוב. The תנא קמא says wine for all. רבי יהודה says each person gets what fits them: wine for men, and clothing for women, according to local taste.
steps.whyThisMatters: Halacha follows this approach: a husband buys his wife clothing or jewelry for יום טוב according to his means, and children get treats.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef teaches:
In Babylonia — with colored clothes,
in Eretz Yisrael — with pressed linen clothes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: בְּבָבֶל — בְּבִגְדֵי צִבְעוֹנִין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Women are made happy with garments: colored ones in בבל, pressed linen in ארץ ישראל

steps.title: Rejoicing with meat when the בית המקדש stood, and with wine today
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא teaches that when the בית המקדש stood, the מצוה of שמחה was fulfilled through eating שלמים meat. Today it is fulfilled through wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says, when the בית המקדש is standing, rejoicing is only with meat, as it says, 'You shall sacrifice שלמים, eat there, and rejoice before ה׳ your God.' Now that the בית המקדש is not standing, rejoicing is only with wine, as it says, 'And wine gladdens the heart of man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about שמחת יום טוב. This one explains that the way to rejoice depends on whether the בית המקדש is standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 6–10 discussed how to make one's family happy. This ברייתא adds a time-based rule: the main form of שמחה used to be eating קרבן שלמים meat, and since there are no קרבנות today, wine takes its place. Each half of the rule has its own פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Rejoicing, here the מצוה of rejoicing on יום טוב
Peace-offerings, קרבנות whose meat the owner eats
And now, meaning in our times

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the basic source for the idea that wine is the main way to fulfill שמחת יום טוב today. It also leads straight into the next topic, the measurement of a cup of wine.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
At the time when the Temple is standing
there is no rejoicing except with meat,
as it says: 'And you shall sacrifice peace-offerings'
'and you shall eat there'
'and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God,'
and now that the Temple is not standing,
there is no rejoicing except with wine,
as it says: 'And wine gladdens the heart of man.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of שמחת יום טוב by adding a rule that depends on whether the בית המקדש is standing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With the בית המקדש, שמחה is through שלמים meat. Without it, שמחה is through wine.

steps.title: The ציפורי vessel used to measure the רביעית
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says the brine-measuring vessel in ציפורי held exactly one לוג of the מקדש, and one quarter of it was used as the רביעית for פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: The brine measuring-cup that was in ציפורי was the same size as the לוג of the מקדש, and with it we measure the רביעית of פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that wine is in focus, the גמרא moves to a practical question: how big is the רביעית, the minimum cup of wine for the ארבע כוסות? רבי יצחק points to a real vessel that was used as the measuring standard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רביעית is a quarter of a לוג. Because the cup in ציפורי held exactly one מקדש-size לוג, people could fill it and divide the liquid into four equal parts to get one רביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: The לוג measure used in the מקדש
A quarter-לוג, the minimum amount of wine for each of the ארבע כוסות

steps.confusionAlert: רביעית is the name of a fixed amount, one quarter of a לוג, not a quarter of whatever vessel you happen to use. This ציפורי vessel works as the tool only because it held exactly one לוג, so a quarter of it equals the רביעית.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
The brine measuring-vessel that was in Tzippori
was like the log of the Temple,
and with it they measure the quarter-log of Pesach.
phrases.notes: They would divide its contents into four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Because wine is the main form of שמחה, the גמרא turns to defining the measure of a cup of wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציפורי brine vessel equals one מקדש לוג, and a quarter of it is the רביעית for פסח.

steps.title: The old טבריה measure used to find the רביעית
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the old 'eighth' measure in טבריה was larger than the newer one by exactly one רביעית, so the difference between the two vessels gives the רביעית for פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The old 'eighth' measure that was in טבריה was larger than this one by a quarter-לוג, and with it we measure the רביעית of פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second real-world way to find the רביעית, using measuring vessels from his own city, טבריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's method works by comparison. If you fill the old vessel and pour it into the newer one, the amount left over in the old vessel is exactly one רביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'eighth' measure, the name of a measuring vessel
The old one, the earlier version

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The old eighth-measure that was in Tiberias
was larger than this one by a quarter-log,
and with it they measure the quarter-log of Pesach.
phrases.notes: The leftover after pouring into the new measure is the רביעית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel statement that offers a second practical way to find the רביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The difference between the old and new 'eighth' measures of טבריה equals one רביעית.

steps.title: The רביעית measured in fingerbreadths
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא gives the size of the Torah's רביעית as a box 2 fingers by 2 fingers, with a height of 2 and 7/10 fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The Torah's רביעית is two fingerbreadths by two fingerbreadths, with a height of two fingerbreadths, plus half a fingerbreadth, plus a fifth of a fingerbreadth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defines the רביעית by measurements of length instead of by a famous vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12–13 tied the רביעית to specific vessels in ציפורי and טבריה. רב חסדא gives a measurement anyone can reproduce anywhere: 2 × 2 × 2.7 fingerbreadths, which comes to 10.8 cubic fingerbreadths.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finger-based measure is the basis for later calculations of the רביעית, which affect כוס של ברכה, the ארבע כוסות, and many other הלכות.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The quarter-log of the Torah
is two fingerbreadths by two fingerbreadths
by a height of two fingerbreadths and half a fingerbreadth
and a fifth of a fingerbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, dimension-based definition of the רביעית.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the מקוה as the source for רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא about טבילה: nothing may separate the body from the water, the water must be a מקוה, and the מקוה must be big enough for the whole body to go in at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'He shall bathe his whole body in the water.' This teaches that nothing may come between his body and the water. 'In the water' means in the water of a מקוה. 'His whole body' means water that his entire body can go into at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing support for רב חסדא's measurement from a ברייתא about the size of a מקוה. This step sets up the calculation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads three lessons out of the פסוק: no חציצה, the water must be a מקוה, and the מקוה must hold the whole body at once. That last lesson leads to a fixed size for a מקוה, and רב חסדא's רביעית will be worked out from that size.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא, introducing a supporting source
Separating, blocking the water from the body (חציצה)
The water of a ritual bath
Fits into them, goes in completely

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא has changed topics to טבילה for its own sake. The מקוה is brought only because its known size is used to calculate the רביעית.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
'And he shall bathe his whole body in the water' —
that nothing should interpose
between his body and the water.
'In the water' — in the water of a mikveh.
'His whole body' —
water that his entire body fits into,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רב חסדא's measurement.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's measurement of the רביעית in fingerbreadths
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that sets the minimum size of a מקוה from the פסוק 'ורחץ במים את כל בשרו'

steps.title: How much water is a valid מקוה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how much water is needed for the whole body to fit in at once. The answer comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much water is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for the exact amount of water in a מקוה. This sets up the answer, which the גמרא will use to calculate רב חסדא's רביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has said that the water must hold the whole body, but it has not yet given a number. This question asks for that number, which is the key to the calculation.

phrases.english: And how much is that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact amount of water implied by the ברייתא's last lesson.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum amount of water in a מקוה, so that the רביעית can be calculated from it.
